State Isolation — Plan of Record

Bugs·budding·accepted·JUL 21, 2026

Dev/test can never sit in production's chair: the one bind-time lock, rebuilt lock-only after PR #1911 failed adversarial review. SI1 gate-leak fix → SI2 the lock → #1912 the wire verbs.

Contents

  • The lock
  • SI1 — padi releases its boot gate on a startup throw
  • SI2 — the lock, rebuilt lock-only
  • Deferred, with its reader —

Kolu’s own dev and test runs could silently compute the production daemon’s identity and then adopt or SIGTERM the live kolu the user is sitting in (#1334; the incident class, in plain words). The first attempt to close it, #1911, was closed after adversarial review: the lock inside it was sound, but only about half the PR was the lock.The review — /perfection-review + /architecture-first-principles C1–C7, 11 hunters over the diff, every finding re-verified by an adversarial refuter — found: ~52% of the 1,483 added lines served the lock; the ephemeral role stamps had no reader in the PR (their consumer, the adopt/kill guard, was rejected to #1912); all 584 added kaval lines existed to write and protect that unread marker; both ssh e2e lanes were broken invisibly (CI has no ssh); and the README overclaimed a bind-time refusal into adopt/SIGTERM immunity. Full verdict on the closed PR. This note is the plan of record for the rebuild.

The lock

One rule, enforced at bind time: the process that opens a state-root must prove it may. Production self-declares (KOLU_ROLE=production, set only by the production nix wrapper locally and by --role production over ssh); every binder resolves its root through one guarded resolver that crashes a non-production launch before it can bind, spawn, adopt, or even create a log directory in production’s root.

The guard refuses a non-production binder three ways, all fail-closed:Fail-closed concretely: an empty, corrupt, or unreadable (EACCES/EIO) marker refuses — absence is only honest as a genuine ENOENT. The root comparison is canonical (realpath down to the deepest existing ancestor), so a symlink alias to the default root — even one whose leaf doesn’t exist yet — is the same root, not a bypass.

  1. The default root (~/.local/state/padi) — production’s by definition, refused with no marker consulted.
  2. An explicit override that is the default root — including symlink aliases.
  3. A relocated root carrying the persistent production marker (#1414) — stamped by production daemons and binders; unreadable or corrupt markers refuse.

SI1 — padi releases its boot gate on a startup throw

The one genuine treasure buried in #1911, extracted as its own small PR that lands first. On master today, padi acquires its single-instance gate before several throwable boot steps and never releases it on a pre-handoff throw — an in-process caller that catches the error can never retry (the gate still names a live pid).

  • Release the gate in the catch after awaiting the partial runtime’s close; use Promise.allSettled for the settle-capture rather than #1911’s hand-rolled discriminated local, and keep the cleanup-failure aggregation.
  • Test trigger must be master-reachable (e.g. a malformed KOLU_DAEMON_BIND_PID), not a role write that only exists in SI2.
  • Done when: the gate file is gone after a boot throw and a same-process re-acquire succeeds, proven by the test.

SI2 — the lock, rebuilt lock-only

Padi + server + nix; zero kaval changes; roughly half of #1911’s size. Rebased on SI1.

Piece Contract
packages/padi/src/role.ts (new, ~250 lines) Everything role-related in one module: selfRole/KOLU_ROLE_ENV; the fail-closed RoleRead marker read; stampPersistentRole exported, the raw production-marker writer module-private; sameRootIdentity; resolveBoundStateRoot + StateRootIsolationError. Refusal messages say “KOLU_ROLE is not ‘production’”, never “unset”.
default.nix --set KOLU_ROLE production on the kolu wrapper.
Server boot · padi daemonMain · stdioBridge Each resolves through the guard; padi guards before the logger opens anything; the stdio bridge becomes async so a refusal reaches bin.ts’s one error channel as the clean one-line message.
--role flag + role threading bin.ts validates --role; the server forwards KOLU_ROLE daemon-to-daemon (never via the PTY allowlist) and threads its own role to remote padis.
Persistent stamp Padi stamps its root at boot; the server binder stamps once per binding (covers pre-fix daemons). Add the missing test that a production boot actually stamps — in #1911 deleting the stamp left the suite green.
ssh lanes remotePadiSsh.test.ts passes --role production (or an isolated --state-root); e2e-ssh-2box launches with KOLU_ROLE=production.
Docs padi --help says the default root is production-only; README claims exactly what the lock does — refuses binding — nothing about adopt/SIGTERM.

Done when, beyond green CI: just e2e-ssh run once and passing — CI has no ssh, so the lane the old PR silently broke is a named, mandatory local gateThis is the path-not-feature rule: the two ssh recipes are the only executions of remotePadiSsh.test.ts, and #1911 shipped 38/38 green while both were broken. A done-criterion that can only be met by running the lane is the fix for that class. — and a bare pnpm dev / vitest / padi on a box with a live production kolu is refused (the #1334 repro, re-run).

Deferred, with its reader — #1912

The adopt/kill wire verbs (kill/killAll/restart on an already-running daemon’s socket) bypass a bind-time lock by construction. The ephemeral role-stamp machinery #1911 carried — the write beside each gate, kaval’s gate-reorder so the stamp is holder-only, the padi→kaval role forwarding — ships there, together with the guard that reads it. Shipping writers ahead of their reader is what made half of #1911 dead weight.

Sequencing

SI1 (small, independent) → SI2 (the lock, closes #1334) → #1912 (wire-verb guard + role stamps, its own review). srid merges each; full /be arc per PR.
